title: Warehouse Configuration (physical layout, v5)
description: Physical layer of a warehouse: building walls, doors, the corridor network, lift stations, delivery spaces, storage slot footprints, and each slot's physical depth. Coordinates are in meters (1 unit = 1m), origin at the bottom-left of the site, +X right, +Y up. This describes what physically exists (the building), not what's currently stocked (see warehouse.content.schema.json). The corridor network is named junctions and corridors listing the junctions they run through: two corridors connect exactly when they name the same junction. Slots and pads state the corridor they are worked from (`access`). A config file is loaded first; its content file (referencing this file's `id` as `warehouseId`) is loaded second and merged in.

units.description: Fixed to meters for now; kept explicit so other units can be supported later without an ambiguous scale.

walls.description: One or more wall loops/polylines. Each is an ordered list of corner points. Supports irregular outlines, notches, and multiple disjoint structures (e.g. a detached annex) by using multiple entries.

doors.description: Openings in a building's wall to the exterior or to another building. Optional — absent in files predating this field, treated as empty.

junctions.description: The corridor network's named points: where corridors meet, end, bend or pass through a door. Names follow the plant's convention (specs.md §5.7), e.g. "13A.CENTRAL+AA", "AA.E", "13A.S".

corridors.description: Named corridors, each the junctions it runs through in order, e.g. aisle "AA", "13A.CENTRAL", the link "13A-12B".

paths.description: Legacy corridor format (polylines connected only by exactly coincident coordinates). Read, and converted to junctions and corridors, when `corridors` is absent; never written.

liftStations.description: Carriage lift stations (fixed 6x2m footprint for now). Optional — absent in files predating this field, treated as empty.

deliverySpaces.description: Delivery spaces (fixed 6x2m footprint, same as liftStation, for now). Optional — absent in files predating this field, treated as empty.

inaccessibleZones.description: Floor areas forklifts can't enter (a lithium store, a tugger-train lane...), drawn hatched. Corridors are laid out around them. Optional — absent in files predating this field, treated as empty.

slotDefaults.description: Applied to every slot for now: its footprint (all slots are the same size) and how high each depth position stacks.

closed.description: If true, an implicit segment connects the last point back to the first, forming a closed polygon. If false, it's an open polyline.

rotationDeg.description: Orientation along the wall it's set into, in degrees — same convention as slot.rotationDeg.

width.description: Opening width in meters. Defaults to the renderer's DOOR_DEFAULT_WIDTH when omitted.

buildingId.description: Which building's wall (a walls[].id of a closed loop) this door is cut into.

leadsTo.description: Another building's id, if this door connects two buildings rather than leading outside.

buildingId.description: The building it stands in (a door's junction: the door's building). Omitted outdoors.

junctions.description: Junction ids, in order along the corridor.

width.description: Corridor width in meters. Defaults to the renderer's PATH_DEFAULT_WIDTH when omitted.

access.description: Where a slot or pad joins the corridor network. Without it the app uses the nearest corridor (in front of a slot).

offset.description: Meters along the corridor from its first junction.

points.description: A point shared with another path's points, or with a door's position, must be an exact coincident coordinate — see the top-level description's graph-readiness note.

width.description: Corridor width in meters. Defaults to the renderer's PATH_DEFAULT_WIDTH when omitted.

buildingIds.description: Usually one building; two for a connector that crosses between buildings.

endpointBuildingIds.description: Cross-building connectors only (buildingIds.length > 1): which building owns points[0] and which owns the last point, in that order.

label.description: What the plan calls the area, e.g. "Lithium", "Zone MU", "Train".

width.description: Footprint size along the slot's local X axis (before rotation), in meters.

height.description: Footprint size along the slot's local Y axis (before rotation), in meters.

width.description: Footprint size along the slot's local X axis (before rotation), in meters.

height.description: Footprint size along the slot's local Y axis (before rotation), in meters — one depth position's.

levels.description: Pallet tiers per depth position, so a slot holds depth x levels pallets: stores, the editor's + Pallet and a loaded stock extract all stop there. Default 3.

id.description: Real WMS location code (e.g. "A01"), used as the unique identifier.

x.description: Center point X coordinate (in meters) when depth is 1. With depth > 1, anchors the frontmost (depth position 0) sub-slot's own full-size footprint instead — additional sub-slots extend the footprint outward from there, so this point doesn't move as depth changes.

y.description: Center point Y coordinate (in meters) when depth is 1. See x for the depth > 1 case.

rotationDeg.description: Counter-clockwise rotation of the slot footprint around its center point, in degrees. 0 = width (slotDefaults.width) along +X, height along +Y. Usually a multiple of 90, but not restricted to one.

depth.description: Number of sub-slot depth positions (front-to-back), each occupying its own full slotDefaults footprint (a depth-3 slot spans 3x the standard footprint, not the standard footprint split three ways). A physical/structural property, independent of what's currently stocked there — see warehouse.content.schema.json for that.

access.description: The corridor the slot is worked from — for a CML import, the aisle its label is written in.
